key_insight: Long tasks may not require long model contexts. Frequent context compaction preserved little-to-no loss in task accuracy across the evaluated long-input and long-horizon tasks.
problem_solved: Generating later tokens becomes increasingly expensive as context grows, with costs reaching up to 7× those of earlier tokens on frontier open-weight models.
method: Frequently compact accumulated context to keep the model's working context short.
Evaluate task accuracy across a broad range of long-input and long-horizon tasks.
Test long-horizon software engineering with at most one action per context, finding that performance does not collapse.
impact: Keeping contexts short could reduce inference costs without materially sacrificing accuracy on the evaluated tasks. Practitioners should consider context-compaction strategies rather than assuming larger context windows are always necessary.
visual_elements: Token-cost chart highlighting the reported up-to-7× cost disparity between earlier and later tokens.
Workflow diagram: task → action → context compaction → next action.
Accuracy comparison graphic showing little-to-no loss with frequent compaction, without inventing numerical scores.
Software engineering timeline illustrating one action per context across a long task.
paper_authors: Peter Belcak, Saurav Muralidharan, Jindong Jiang, Yonggan Fu, Wonmin Byeon
